title: usage-calc
summary: A command-line tool that reads the GitHub Copilot CLI's local request ledger and publishes what an AI-assisted project cost in money, tokens, model time and human time as one self-contained page.

narrative.problem: Almost every public claim about what AI-assisted work costs rests on an invented denominator: a remembered number of hours, a guessed number of requests, a rate nobody published.
narrative.decision: It reads the per-request SQLite ledger the Copilot CLI writes as it works, with the model, token counts, duration and billed price, and refuses to print a total it cannot reconcile; the output is a single HTML page with no CDN, build step or server.
narrative.tradeoff: The ledger is per machine, so a dashboard built on one laptop is a floor, not a total: other machines must be exported and merged by hand, and a machine nobody remembers stays invisible.
narrative.limitation: The dollar figure is a list-price equivalent, not a bill; person time is an inferred residual that cannot distinguish thinking from lunch; the energy panel is an estimate whose bracket spans a factor of 24; and nothing measures whether the output was worth having.

images.caption: The data source: a ledger written as the work happened, carrying the model, tokens, duration and billed price of every request.

images.caption: A measured result from a real two-machine project: a single machine's ledger understated the project-wide cost and request count.

images.caption: How the dashboard labels its numbers: model time is measured, person time is inferred, and the page always says which is which.
